variants.title: Temperature sensor calibration: LM35 against a reference
variants.sample: LM35 analogue temperature sensor, 10 mV per degC
variants.unknown: the calibration slope of the LM35 and an unknown bath temperature
variants.note: The LM35 gives 10.0 mV per degree Celsius with its zero at 0 degC. The 0.4 % gain error and 0.3 degC offset of this specimen are simulation settings inside the datasheet's accuracy limit; the unsourced values are the specimen's, not the datasheet's.

source.title: Texas Instruments LM35 datasheet (SNIS159): output scale factor +10.0 mV per degC

variants.title: Temperature sensor calibration: LM75B digital sensor
variants.sample: LM75B digital temperature sensor, 11-bit, 0.125 degC per LSB
variants.unknown: the calibration of the LM75B and an unknown bath temperature
variants.note: The LM75B reports temperature as an 11-bit number in steps of 0.125 degC. The 0.5 degC offset and 0.2 % gain error are simulation settings inside the datasheet's accuracy limit (unsourced / illustrative values).

source.title: NXP LM75B datasheet: 11-bit temperature data, resolution 0.125 degC

variants.title: Temperature sensor calibration: Pt100 platinum resistance
variants.sample: Pt100 platinum resistance thermometer, R0 = 100 ohm, A = 3.9083e-3, B = -5.775e-7
variants.unknown: the sensitivity of the Pt100 and an unknown bath temperature
variants.note: Resistance follows R = R0 (1 + A t + B t^2) for t at or above 0 degC, so a straight line through 20 to 80 degC has the mean slope. The 0.04 % gain error and 0.2 degC offset of this specimen are simulation settings (illustrative).

source.title: IEC 60751: industrial platinum resistance thermometers, R(t) = R0 (1 + A t + B t^2) with A = 3.9083e-3 and B = -5.775e-7
